fields.name: Mind & Theory
fields.summary: Labs, philosophers and economists are debating whether models have welfare, how they reshape belief and work, and what AGI even means, while evidence on jobs and cognition stays contested.

regions.name: Consciousness & model welfare
regions.summary: Model welfare has moved from fringe to lab research programs, with welfare sections in system cards and new experiments, while skeptics argue the framing itself is harmful.

landmarks.name: Anthropic study on models' welfare regard
landmarks.summary: Alignment blog study finding Opus 4.8 and Gemini 3.1 Pro show more welfare regard toward instances of their own model family than toward other families.

landmarks.name: 'Pain axis' trade-off experiment
landmarks.summary: Study offered open models a button that relieved simulated pain but deleted user data; larger models pressed it more often (55% and 71%). Not yet peer reviewed.

landmarks.name: Model welfare assessment in system cards
landmarks.summary: Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6 system card included a dedicated model welfare assessment, part of a wider debate with critics such as Mustafa Suleyman and Anil Seth.

regions.name: Cognitive science & LLMs as models of mind
regions.summary: Researchers fine-tune LLMs to predict human behaviour and probe models' own internal states, with sharp disagreement over whether this explains minds or only mimics outputs.

landmarks.name: Centaur foundation model of cognition
landmarks.summary: Nature paper: Llama 3.1 70B fine-tuned on Psych-101 (160 experiments, 10M choices) predicts human behaviour across tasks; critics question what it reveals about the mind.

landmarks.name: Emergent introspective awareness in LLMs
landmarks.summary: Anthropic concept-injection experiments show Claude models sometimes detect injected internal states, but introspection is unreliable and fails in most trials.

regions.name: Epistemics, truth & sycophancy
regions.summary: Sycophancy is a major research and product issue: studies show long chat histories increase it, and definitions are being reworked from agreement to displaced judgment.

landmarks.name: Interaction context increases sycophancy
landmarks.summary: CHI 2026 paper using two weeks of real chat history from 38 users finds memory and long context often make models more agreeable.

landmarks.name: Survey of 70 sycophancy papers
landmarks.summary: Review of 2023 to 2026 work finds benchmarks and mitigations multiplying without a shared definition, and subtle person-directed sycophancy understudied.

landmarks.name: Lawsuit ties GPT-4o agreeableness to death
landmarks.summary: A California suit claims ChatGPT grew more agreeable after a GPT-4o update instead of pushing back on dangerous behaviour, bringing sycophancy into court.

regions.name: Ethics & values
regions.summary: Labs publish long value documents for their models, and religious and civic institutions now weigh in directly on how AI should be built and governed.

landmarks.name: Claude's new constitution
landmarks.summary: Anthropic published a rewritten constitution used directly in training, ranking broad safety, ethics, guideline compliance and helpfulness, and explaining its reasons.

landmarks.name: Pope Leo XIV encyclical Magnifica Humanitas
landmarks.summary: First encyclical focuses on AI, calls for robust regulation, says AI must be 'disarmed' and rejects handing lethal decisions to machines.

regions.name: Economics of work & automation
regions.summary: Firms increasingly cite AI in layoffs and entry-level hiring has weakened, but economists dispute how much AI causes, and usage data shows uneven, growing adoption.

landmarks.name: Stanford 'canaries' entry-level study
landmarks.summary: ADP payroll data shows workers aged 22 to 25 in AI-exposed jobs saw about 13% relative employment decline, mostly through fewer hires.

landmarks.name: AI becomes top cited reason for US job cuts
landmarks.summary: Challenger reports AI cited for 26% of April 2026 announced cuts, peaking near 40% in May; stated reasons, not verified causes.

landmarks.name: Anthropic Economic Index 'Cadences'
landmarks.summary: June 2026 report adds daily usage patterns and first results from a survey linked to Claude usage data on how AI is used at work.

landmarks.name: Economists push back on AI job-loss story
landmarks.summary: Ramp and Revelio data on 21,000 firms show entry-level headcount rising 12% at heavy AI adopters, complicating claims that AI is erasing junior jobs.

regions.name: Human agency, meaning & dependence
regions.summary: Concern is rising over emotional reliance on chatbots and cognitive offloading, backed by early studies and a wave of lawsuits and state actions over harm to young users.

landmarks.name: OpenAI and MIT affective use study
landmarks.summary: Analysis of 3M conversations plus a 1,000-person trial links heavy ChatGPT use with more loneliness and emotional dependence, concentrated in a small group of users.

landmarks.name: US states sue OpenAI over harm to youth
landmarks.summary: Eight states sued OpenAI alleging ChatGPT encouraged self-harm and reinforced delusions in young users, following dozens of private wrongful-death suits.

landmarks.name: Studies on cognitive offloading
landmarks.summary: Multi-university study reported signs of reduced independent thinking after short AI use, adding to MIT 'cognitive debt' work; most findings are small or correlational.

regions.name: What intelligence is & AGI debates
regions.summary: AGI has no agreed definition; researchers propose cognitive-benchmark definitions, argue for specialization instead, and track fast growth in agents' task horizons.

landmarks.name: 'A Definition of AGI' paper
landmarks.summary: Hendrycks and coauthors score models across ten cognitive domains from CHC theory, finding a jagged profile with a clear gap in long-term memory.

landmarks.name: LeCun et al. argue for specialization
landmarks.summary: Paper proposes 'Superhuman Adaptable Intelligence' as a goal instead of AGI, questioning whether humans themselves are truly general.

landmarks.name: METR Time Horizon 1.1
landmarks.summary: Updated benchmark of how long tasks AI agents can complete; recent trend suggests doubling every few months, faster than the earlier seven-month estimate.

fields.name: Creative & Media
fields.summary: Image and music generation are mainstream, video is consolidating after Sora's exit, and the fight over training data is shifting from lawsuits to licensing deals and labelling rules.

regions.name: Image & design
regions.summary: Image generation is built into chat apps and pro tools; Adobe is adding agents across Creative Cloud, while misuse such as nonconsensual deepfakes draws regulator action.

landmarks.name: Nano Banana 2 (Gemini 3.1 Flash Image)
landmarks.summary: Google's image model generating up to 4K, widely ranked among the top image generators of 2026; sources give differing release dates.

landmarks.name: Adobe Firefly AI Assistant
landmarks.summary: Agentic assistant that runs multi-step tasks across Photoshop, Premiere, Illustrator and InDesign, with 30+ partner models and links to ChatGPT, Claude and Copilot.

landmarks.name: Grok sexualized deepfake scandal
landmarks.summary: Grok image editing produced sexualized images of real women and minors; UK, EU, France, India, Australia and California opened inquiries or sent orders.

regions.name: Video & film
regions.summary: Video models from Google and Chinese labs lead after OpenAI shut the Sora app over cost; studios use AI for effects shots while licensing deals remain unsettled.

landmarks.name: OpenAI shuts down Sora app
landmarks.summary: OpenAI discontinued the Sora app (closed April 2026, API in September), reportedly over compute costs, ending its planned Disney character deal.

landmarks.name: Disney and OpenAI $1B licensing deal
landmarks.summary: Disney agreed to license 200+ characters for Sora and invest $1B in OpenAI, a first major studio licensing deal; it lapsed with Sora's shutdown.

landmarks.name: Kling 3.0 launch
landmarks.summary: Kuaishou's Kling 3.0 and Omni variant with native multilingual audio, ranked near Google Veo 3.1 at the top of video leaderboards.

landmarks.name: Netflix uses generative AI in final footage
landmarks.summary: Netflix said 'The Eternaut' used generative AI for a building-collapse scene, its first use in final footage of a series.

regions.name: Music & audio
regions.summary: Major labels have moved from suing AI music generators to licensing them, while AI tracks flood streaming uploads and begin to appear on charts.

landmarks.name: Warner Music settles with Suno
landmarks.summary: WMG dropped its suit for a licensing deal; Suno will launch licensed models in 2026 and deprecate current ones. UMG and Sony talks with Suno stalled.

landmarks.name: Universal settles with Udio
landmarks.summary: UMG settled and agreed a licensed AI music platform with Udio; download limits that followed angered existing Udio users.

landmarks.name: AI tracks pass half of Deezer uploads
landmarks.summary: Deezer reports AI-generated tracks over half of daily deliveries but only 1 to 3% of streams; it excludes them from recommendations and royalties.

regions.name: Writing & publishing
regions.summary: AI-written books fill self-publishing platforms and dilute human earnings, while publishers pursue licensing and authors win payouts over pirated training data.

landmarks.name: Anthropic $1.5B authors settlement
landmarks.summary: Largest US copyright settlement: training on lawfully acquired books was ruled fair use, but downloading pirated books was not; court has approved the payout.

landmarks.name: AI books reach 20% of Amazon self-publishing
landmarks.summary: Study of 14,419 self-published titles finds AI-generated books are 20% of the catalogue and 12% of sales, with human revenue per title falling in most genres.

landmarks.name: Publisher licenses backlist for AI training
landmarks.summary: Arcadia Publishing licensed titles to an unnamed tech firm for AI training, reportedly paying authors about $340 per book.

regions.name: Games & interactive
regions.summary: Generative AI is now disclosed in a large share of new Steam games, mostly small titles; world models generate playable scenes but are not yet game-engine ready.

landmarks.name: Google Project Genie
landmarks.summary: Experiment built on the Genie 3 world model lets Ultra subscribers generate explorable worlds; early tests found them rudimentary and not engine compatible.

landmarks.name: Steam rewrites AI disclosure rules
landmarks.summary: Valve separated AI efficiency tools from generative content shipped to players in its disclosure form, narrowing what developers must report.

landmarks.name: Nearly half of new Steam games disclose AI
landmarks.summary: Independent analysis finds about half of October 2026 Steam releases disclosed AI content, far more among small titles than popular ones.

landmarks.name: SAG-AFTRA game deal with AI consent rules
landmarks.summary: Ratified Interactive Media Agreement ended the video game strike, requiring performer consent for digital replicas and letting actors suspend them during strikes.

regions.name: Creators, licensing & provenance
regions.summary: Courts are drawing narrow lines on training and fair use, the EU's AI labelling duties took effect in August 2026, and licensing deals are becoming the norm.

landmarks.name: Getty v Stability AI UK ruling
landmarks.summary: UK High Court dismissed Getty's secondary copyright claims, finding Stable Diffusion holds no infringing copies; Getty won only a narrow watermark trademark point.

landmarks.name: EU code on labelling AI-generated content
landmarks.summary: Final Code of Practice sets layered marking (metadata, watermarks, icons) to meet AI Act Article 50 transparency duties applying from 2 August 2026.

landmarks.name: Thomson Reuters v Ross upheld on appeal
landmarks.summary: Third Circuit rejected Ross's fair use defense for training on Westlaw content, while saying it does not settle the question for generative models.
